The Na+‐K‐ATPase plays an important role in the development of mouse embryos in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the effects of various potassium (K+) concentrations on the culture of fertilized mouse ova to blastocysts and the effects of low concentrations of K+ or ouabain on the development of the mouse preimplantational embryo.
the effect of potassium on the development of mouse embryos cultured in vitro.
the effects of various conditions that inhibit the enzyme Na‐K‐ATPase on the development of mouse zygote to the blastocysts stage in vitro.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Na+‐ATP‐ase is not the sole factor responsible for the regulation of the Na+ and K+ concentrations in the preimplantion mouse embryo.
the Na+‐dependent transport system is not the main factor determining the fate of the embryo in the preimplantational phase.
the Na+‐dependent transport of amino acids is an essential process in the preimplantion mouse embryo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the preimplantational development is a process of differentiation of the embryo from the zygote to the blastocysts.
the inhibition of the Na‐K‐ATPase enzyme during the 2‐cell stage in mice is beneficial for further development of the embryo to the blastocysts stage.
